data.title: Changzhou Microintelligence seeks up to $74.62 million in revived Hong Kong IPO
data.description:
China-based Changzhou Microintelligence (3275.HK) is looking to raise up to HK$584.9 million ($74.62 million) through its Hong Kong initial public offering to fund research and development, an exchange filing showed on Monday.

The industrial robot maker has set an indicative offer price range of HK$12.07 to HK$15.69 per share.

Here are some details:

  • The company withdrew its earlier Hong Kong IPO in October, which had sought to raise up to HK$799.9 million, citing prevailing market conditions

  • Changzhou Microintelligence shelved its initial listing plans amid a global technology selloff driven by concerns over the sustainability of the AI spending boom and whether returns would justify heavy investment across the sector

  • The new offering comprises 37.3 million H shares, of which about 33.5 million will be allocated to international investors

  • More than 60% of the proceeds will be used to develop the company's core technologies, with a focus on enhancing the intelligence and performance of its embodied intelligent industrial robot (EIIR) products

  • The company expects H shares to start trading on December 4

  • The new prospectus includes a downward price adjustment mechanism that would allow the offer price to be reduced to as low as HK$10.87 per share if market conditions warrant

($1 = 7.8389 Hong Kong dollars)

data.title: BHP unveils plans to double copper output in South Australia by 2040
data.description:
BHP , the world's top copper miner, revealed plans on Monday to double its South Australian copper production by 2040 at a cost of up to $18.1 billion, with a final investment decision due in the first half of next year.

BHP said it had found a path to raise annual copper production from the operations to 650,000 metric tons, with investment of $14.2 billion to $18.1 billion. That would boost copper production from the region, which BHP says is the world's second-biggest for copper, and take it close to the capacity of the world's largest copper mine, Escondida in Chile.

The world's largest listed miner aims to produce 2 million tons of the metal, which is key to electrification, from its global operations by the middle of the next decade, and expects the Copper South Australia operations to deliver around one third of its copper growth to 2035.

When including expected byproducts such as uranium, gold and silver from Copper SA, BHP said that global production will be equivalent to 2.5 million tons of copper per year.

The Copper SA operations include Olympic Dam and the Carrapateena and Prominent Hill mines, which it acquired in 2023, and a 2018 discovery at Ankata, which was originally named Oak Dam.

BHP said it expects consolidation, the introduction of block caving, which is a type of bulk mining, and extended processing to significantly cut operating costs.

As part of the expansion, BHP will increase the capacity of its uranium processing plant to increase production by around half to 5,000 to 6,000 tons a year.

($1 = 1.5117 Australian dollars)

data.title: Development of BHP's Copper South Australia operations
data.description:
BHP , the world's top copper miner, unveiled plans on Monday to double its South Australian copper production by 2040 at a cost of up to $18.1 billion, with a final investment decision due in the first half of next year.

The centrepiece of that plan, Olympic Dam, was intended to become a top-tier growth engine after BHP took over Western Mining Corporation in 2005. There have been multiple expansion concepts since then, but so far none of them has been executed.

1975 - Western Mining Corp discovers the Olympic Dam mineral deposit in the state of South Australia.

1979 - Joint venture formed with BP Group to develop the project.

1988 - Underground mining starts at an annual rate of 45,000 metric tons of copper, plus byproducts uranium oxide, gold and silver.

1995 - After a series of optimisation projects, Olympic Dam is producing 170,000 metric tons a year of copper and associated byproducts. It has conditional approval to increase that to 350,000 tons.

2005 - BHP acquires WMC, and with it Olympic Dam, for about A$9.2 billion.

2009 - BHP, under CEO Marius Kloppers, proposes a giant open-pit expansion and releases a draft environmental impact study, with plans to lift production by about 515,000 tons of copper per year above existing output.

2011 - The proposed expansion receives major approvals. Industry estimates at the time put the project cost at around $30 billion, which would have made it one of the world's largest mining developments.

2012 - BHP shelves the open-pit expansion. Kloppers says the project had become too costly, linking the decision to weaker commodity markets and the need for stricter capital allocation. The estimated capital bill remained around $30 billion.

2017 - BHP confirms it is investigating a brownfield expansion plan for Olympic Dam under CEO Andrew Mackenzie, which would raise production to 450,000 tons per year of copper from the mid-2020s.

2018 - BHP announces the discovery of the Oak Dam West copper-gold-uranium deposit about 65 km (40 miles) southeast of Olympic Dam, after drilling intersects one of the best copper discoveries in Australia in decades.

2019 - BHP's brownfield expansion plan is declared a major development by South Australia.

2020 - Mike Henry takes the helm of the world's biggest miner and BHP abandons the Olympic Dam expansion plan due to high costs. Instead, it focuses on a debottlenecking strategy which backs incremental investments in smelter, refinery and underground mine capacity rather than a multi-decade open-pit project.

2023 - BHP acquires Australian copper miner OZ Minerals for around A$9.6 billion and creates Copper South Australia by combining Olympic Dam with the former OZ Minerals assets, Prominent Hill and Carrapateena, which are in the same region.

2024-2026 - BHP focuses on lifting production across Copper South Australia through smelter expansion studies, mine growth and exploration, as well as integration of the three asset hubs.

2027 - BHP is due to make a final investment decision on the expansion project.

2063 - Planned closure of the operations.

data.title: Japan's wealthy bank accounts over JPY100mn jump 4.2%
data.description:
Japan had 154,200 personal bank accounts holding at least JPY100mn ($629,000) at the end of September, a 4.2% rise on the previous year, Jiji Press reported on November 21, citing a Bank of Japan survey.

Money in these large accounts is growing faster than household savings as a whole. Jiji Press attributed the trend to higher asset values driven by rising share prices, among other factors, and said wealth was becoming more concentrated among Japan's richest savers.

Combined balances in the accounts grew 5.0% year on year to JPY32.72 trillion. Total deposits held by individuals rose 1.3% over the same period.

The number of such accounts has increased 3.6-fold since the end of September 2000, the earliest point for which comparable figures exist.

Most of the large accounts fell into the lowest bracket covered by the survey. Some 135,800 held between JPY100mn and JPY300mn, while 15,600 contained from JPY300mn up to JPY1bn. Another 2,800 accounts had balances of JPY1bn or more.

data.title: Faraday Future CEO YT Jia Shares Weekly Update: FFAI’s Remediation of Nine Previously Identified Material Weaknesses in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting; FFR’s Multiple Strategic Education Partnerships and Robots Sales with Public Schools
data.description:
Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. () (“Faraday Future”, “FF” or the “Company”), a California-based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today shared a weekly business update from YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF and FFR.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261122557721/en/

Faraday Future CEO YT Jia Shares Weekly Update: FFAI’s Remediation of Nine Previously Identified Material Weaknesses in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting; FFR’s Multiple Strategic Education Partnerships and Robots Sales with Public Schools

“Welcome to my 82nd weekly report. Let me start with three major breakthroughs for FFR’s education ecosystem in U.S. K–12 and career education. First, FFR is now an approved robotics supplier to a public school district that is considered top-tier both nationally and within California. We’ve cleared the district’s review and joined its procurement platform. That means more than 1,000 schools in the district can now purchase FFR robots and our education productivity solutions directly. This week, the district’s career education center led the way by purchasing several robots, including FX Navi and Aegis EDU. We hope the project will serve as a model for a broader rollout across the district.

Second, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with another public school district, one of California’s leading districts. The district has also purchased robot devices including Master Mini and Aegis EDU. Third, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with an additional major public school district in Los Angeles.

The second and third partnerships both cover K–12 through adult education. We’ll work with the two districts to develop curricula together, set up innovation labs, create career and technical education pathways, train teachers, and give students hands-on experience. Together, we’ll explore how Physical AI education can connect what students learn in the classroom with further study, real-world practice, and career development. These two collaborations both renew automatically at the end of their terms. With these frameworks in place, we can move future projects forward quickly through a streamlined process.

Outside of California, we are also moving forward with strategic partnerships and sales in robotics education across multiple school districts in four other states: New York, Pennsylvania, Florida, and Texas. FFR pioneered K–12 robotics education in the U.S., and we’re now No. 1 in the industry. The progress we’ve made on strategic partnerships and robot purchases across these three leading districts matters to FFR and to the whole industry. Let me share four reasons why:

First, it’s a big step forward for our education ecosystem. By working with major school districts as strategic partners at the school district level, we can work directly with the U.S. public education system to build Physical AI education pathways that connect K–12 learning, technical skills training, and future careers.

Second, these projects give us a model for replicating at scale nationwide. The U.S. has more than 13,000 regular public-school districts. Across the country, about 130,000 public and private K–12 schools serve roughly 53 million students. That’s a large market, with opportunities across robot devices, curricula, teacher training, and ongoing services. We’ll learn from our first projects with leading districts, turn what works into a repeatable model, and gradually roll it out to across the country.

Third, it helps us move faster on our Four-Core Full-Stack AI business in education and speeds up the evolutionary flywheel. In real classrooms, we can deploy robot devices, develop Skills and solutions, and collect data in line with applicable requirements. That data helps us keep improving our Education Brain.

Fourth, it helps transform U.S. education in the Physical AI era. By making robots a regular part of teaching and hands-on learning, we can prepare the next generation of developers and skilled workers for the new era. As FFR’s profile in the industry grows, we’ve received invitations from schools, universities, and school districts to take part in academic discussions and major exhibitions. I’ll share more about those with you in future reports.

Regarding corporate governance, this week we welcomed Carolyn Kissane to FFR’s board as an independent director. Carolyn is the associate dean of New York University’s Center for Global Affairs. She brings years of experience in higher education and knows how to bring universities, researchers, and companies together. Carolyn could help us grow our robotics education ecosystem, reach more developers, and build more industry partnerships. She’ll also help us bring technology, talent, industry, and capital together. That will help us put our Four-Core Full-Stack AI strategy to work faster across all four industry ecosystems.

We also held our Middle East launch in Dubai this week. Six of our robots made their debut in the region. With our local partners, we showed five ways to put robots to work across our four industry ecosystems: education, security and inspection, entertainment, healthcare, and interactive sports. Together, we’re opening a new chapter for Physical AI in the Middle East. We’ll share a video from Dubai next week, so stay tuned.

For FFAI: it released its Q3 results this week. I want to highlight an important step we’ve taken on financial management and internal controls. After evaluating and testing the controls, FFAI management concluded that, as of September 30, 2026, FFAI had corrected all nine previously identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting. Management also concluded that the related controls were operating effectively. FFAI has spent nearly two years improving FFAI’s financial management and internal controls. This progress puts us in a stronger position to meet our obligations as a public company, raise capital, and rebuild trust with investors. It also gives us a stronger foundation to grow and create value through our shared Robotaxi network, AI VisiCabin operations, and Physical AI investment and holdings business. All right, thanks for tuning in. I’ll see you next week!”

ABOUT FARADAY FUTURE

Founded in 2014, Faraday Future (FF) is a U.S.-based Physical AI ecosystem company dedicated to merging the future of robotics and mobility solutions through AI innovation and technologies. Following the completion of the transfer of its robotics business to FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (FFR), Faraday Future is upgrading into a Robotaxi and EAI Cabin (Intelligent cabin) shared mobility operations company and a Physical AI investment holding company. Evolving its automotive business from an EV manufacturer to a Robotaxi Sharing Network and AI Visicabin technology operator. FF aims to advance its “Four Future Trends” concept, once again helping to drive automotive industry transformation. For more information, please visit Faraday Future's official website: https://www.ff.com/

Some of today’s updates are forward-looking, and actual results may differ materially. The risk factors are in our SEC filings. data.title: LTR Pharma Advances US Commercial Rollout of ROXUS Intranasal ED Treatment
data.description:
LTR Pharma has issued more than 500 bottles of rapid-onset intranasal erectile dysfunction (ED) treatment ROXUS since its US launch in October under the patient-specific 503A regulatory pathway.

Prescriptions have been fulfilled across 43 US states through direct-to-consumer telehealth company Shed Holdings (under a distribution agreement signed in July) and Strive Compounding Pharmacy.

Shed is leading digital patient acquisition through an initial phase that includes assessing patient experience, retention, and repeat activity to inform broader scaling of marketing activity.

As ROXUS is an on-demand treatment, patient usage and re-order timing will vary and LTR believes repeat purchasing and retention trends will become clearer as the initial cohorts mature.

LTR has invoiced Strive and received its first US revenue and prescribing, fulfilment, invoicing and payment infrastructure now operational.

Advancing Customer Reach

Alongside Shed, LTR is developing a separate healthcare professional and direct-to-clinic channel that will allow clinics to prescribe ROXUS for eligible patients while Strive Pharmacy fulfils the prescriptions.

Work to enable ROXUS within established electronic prescribing workflows has progressed, including connectivity through electronic prescribing network Surescripts, which is used by 1.39 million prescribers and 98.3% of US pharmacies.

Initial prescribing has commenced through a small number of clinics including Prime Institute in Florida and Urology Partners in North Texas.

These clinics are operated by LTR scientific advisory board members Dr Amy Pearlman and Dr Andrew Sun, respectively.

LTR is also continuing clinician education following its attendance at the Sexual Medicine Society of North America annual scientific meeting in October, where it engaged with US specialists regarding intranasal PDE5 therapy, administration and Australian real-world experience.

Valuable Market Insights

LTR executive chair Lee Rodne said the fulfillment milestone demonstrated the geographical reach and licensure of the company’s partner network.

“Reaching more than 500 bottles is an encouraging early milestone and the initial US rollout gives us valuable insights into demand, treatment response, and the patient experience,” he said.

“It has reinforced the importance of first-use education and administration guidance, consistent with our experience in Australia, and we are working closely with Shed and Strive to apply these learnings to patient education, onboarding, and provider support before progressively scaling commercial activity.”

“Our focus at this stage is establishing the patient experience, retention and prescribing pathways required to support sustainable broader adoption.”

Indian Patent Granted

The Indian Patent Office has granted LTR with a patent to protect defined formulation characteristics of the intranasal technology supporting lead products SPONTAN and ROXUS through to May 2041.

The fast-acting intranasal sprays enable onset of action in 10 minutes or less, compared with 60 minutes for the 20 milligram oral vardenafil tablet.

“The grant of this patent in India is a positive milestone for LTR Pharma, further strengthening the intellectual property portfolio supporting SPONTAN and ROXUS,” Mr Rodne said.

“Protecting our intellectual property remains an important part of our strategy as we advance our clinical and commercial programs.”

data.title: South Korea's education minister quits over exam cheating chaos
data.description:
South Korean Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday, taking responsibility for confusion caused by last-minute measures to prevent AI-assisted cheating in the country's high-stakes college entrance examination held last week.

  • President Lee Jae Myung accepted the resignation within an hour and ordered a comprehensive review of national exam management and related laws.

  • The government rushed out tighter restrictions after the top scorer in a national tax-accountant examination admitted using a miniature camera, a smartphone and artificial intelligence to cheat.

  • During the eight-hour exam, authorities restricted Wi-Fi, checked glasses and clothing buttons for hidden devices, and issued nationwide alerts to detect concealed phones.

  • More than 550,000 students registered for the test, which plays a major role in admission to the country's top universities.

  • Choi acknowledged that inadequate preparation and repeated rule changes had inconvenienced students and officials.

  • He also faced criticism after saying that, because of his age, he did not think he could detect AI-assisted cheating.

  • The heightened precautions last week uncovered dozens of prohibited mobile phones, although it was unclear whether all were intended for cheating.

data.title: US futures bounce while Asia markets brace for AI wipeout
data.description:
US stock futures attempted a recovery on Monday, while Asian markets slid and authorities around the region readied support measures after a withering wipeout last week for tech and chip stocks at the centre of the AI boom.

Investors are questioning whether the vast sums of mostly borrowed money spent building data centres to power AI models will generate returns fast enough to repay lenders and big enough to justify some of the high stock prices.

Last week's 10% drop in the Nasdaq was its largest weekly drop since pandemic panic gripped markets in March 2020.

Nasdaq 100 futures bounced nearly 3% in early trade on Monday, and S&P 500 futures rose by 2%.

South Korea's chip-heavy KOSPI dropped more than 3% in the first few minutes of morning trade.

Japan markets are closed for a holiday on Monday but futures indicate selling pressure, while Hang Seng futures (HSIc1) also point to a fall. Australian stocks were slightly lower.

The "AI trade" has for several years lifted a wide range of stocks, from switch and cable makers to electricity generators and the manufacturers of anything in the computing supply chain, but they have been under pressure in recent months from rising interest rates.

AI-related shares took a particularly sharp downturn last week as the exit of Jensen Huang, the Nvidia CEO nicknamed the "godfather of AI", and the faltering debut of AI company Anthropic , which closed 8.5% lower on its first full day of trading, pointed to a souring mood.

Taiwanese shares TWSE:TAIEX were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly fall since 1990, and Friday's 10% drop for the Philadelphia semiconductor index points to more pain for Asia's chip-heavy markets, especially in Taiwan and South Korea.

Taiwan's financial regulator on Saturday ordered a further tightening of short-selling rules for stocks, while in China stock exchanges announced a batch of support measures such as easing requirements for margin financing.

South Korea will be ready to deploy market stabilisation funds immediately should the market continue to fall, the finance ministry said on Sunday, after the benchmark index last week slumped to 10-month lows.

data.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Flash PMI Data to Provide Gauge on Economic Growth
data.description:
By Dow Jones Newswires staff

Below are the most important global events likely to affect FX and bond markets in the week starting Nov. 23.

November's flash purchasing managers' surveys for the U.S., eurozone and U.K. will be among the key events. The surveys are an important measure of economic activity and could signal whether there is scope for the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of England to raise interest rates further.

In the U.S, markets will also be closely monitoring Personal Consumption Expenditures price data, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure.

In the Asia-Pacific region, South Korea's interest-rate decision will lead the week, with most analysts expecting a quarter-point increase as strong chip exports fuel growth and inflation remains above target. Inflation data from Australia and Tokyo, along with remarks from a Bank of Japan policy board member, could shape expectations for rate increases in both countries.

China will report October industrial profits as investors watch for Beijing's response to tighter U.S. chip export restrictions.

U.S.

U.S. economic activity and inflation will help investors gauge the path of interest rates in a week shortened by a major holiday.

November's flash manufacturing and services PMI numbers are on tap Monday, as well as a speech by New York Federal Reserve President John Williams at the University of Mount Saint Vincent.

September housing indicators are likely to draw attention Tuesday, as elevated mortgage rates weigh on the sector.

The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index is also scheduled for Tuesday, as consumption continues to be a source of strength for the U.S. economy.

A second estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product growth is due Wednesday. The same day will bring the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures, as consumer prices keep rising faster than the 2% annual pace targeted by the central bank.

"The main message from the report is likely to be that pressure on goods prices is growing," economists at the Investment Institute by UniCredit said in a note. "Overall, October PCE data are likely to keep the Fed firmly on a hiking trajectory."

Durable goods orders, initial jobless claims and new home sales data are also due Wednesday along with the Summary of Commentary on Current Economic Conditions by Federal Reserve District, known as the Beige Book.

Markets will be closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving Holiday and will close early on Friday.

U.K.

The U.K. will have a relatively light data release calendar. The November flash estimate purchasing managers' index survey on Monday is the main event.

The U.K. composite PMI, a measure of manufacturing and services activity, rose to 52.9 in October, up from 52.0 in September and the highest reading since February.

"For the November report we imagine that the PMIs ticked higher again," Investec economists said in a note.

Activity might have received a boost from the absence of significant tax increases in the U.K. budget in October as some had feared, they said. U.S. President Trump refraining from renewed large-scale attacks on Iran following the midterm elections might have also helped, not least by helping to lower crude prices, they said. Investec forecasts the composite PMI will rise to 53.1 in November.

Elsewhere, the CBI distributive trades survey is due on Wednesday.

The U.K., meanwhile, plans to sell September 2049 index-linked gilt through syndicated sale, subject to demand and market conditions.

Eurozone

German, French and wider eurozone flash purchasing managers' surveys for November are due on Monday. The eurozone composite purchasing managers index, a measure of manufacturing and services activity, fell to a four-month low of 51.7 in October from 53.1 in September but remained above the 50 level that separates an expansion from a contraction.

"We expect to see some mild weakness in the euro-area PMIs, reflecting the challenging environment for energy markets and tighter financial conditions in Europe," RBC Capital Markets strategists said in a note.

On Tuesday, the German ifo business confidence survey for November will be released. That will be followed by the final third-quarter German gross domestic product report on Wednesday and GfK German consumer confidence survey for December on Thursday.

French and Spanish inflation data for November will be published Friday along with November German labor market data and the European Commission's business confidence survey.

Japan

Bank of Japan policy board member Naoki Tamura will meet with local leaders in the Yamanashi prefecture on Thursday. Investors will watch his remarks for clues on when the central bank might raise rates again.

Tokyo's November consumer-price data are due Friday. The figures are an early indicator of nationwide inflation, and a pickup could strengthen expectations for a rate increase.

BOJ Gov. Kazuo Ueda recently stressed the importance of keeping underlying inflation around the central bank's 2% target. He said inflation excluding fresh food is likely to rise well above 2% as companies pass on higher labor costs, oil prices remain high and the yen stays weak.

The Ministry of Finance will auction about 300 billion yen of 40-year government bonds on Wednesday, reopening an issue first sold in May. The sale could draw demand from insurers and pension funds seeking long-dated debt.

The BOJ is scheduled to buy government bonds in three maturity ranges on Thursday, including those with more than three and up to five years remaining and those with more than 10 and up to 25 years remaining.

Japanese markets will be closed Monday for a national holiday.

China

A thin data slate awaits in China. The sole release of note drops Friday, which will show how China's industrial firms fared in October.

Economists will look at the figures to see if industrial profit growth held up last month after surging in September. Spending tied to artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure has been a key driver of profits over the year, though that hasn't benefited all sectors evenly.

Focus will also be on any potential announcements from Beijing after Xi Jinping's meetings with Trump didn't yield much in the way of progress on key trade and geopolitical issues. Markets will be watching ministry statements closely after Chinese officials warned of potential countermeasures to U.S. moves to tighten chip-export restrictions.

Australia / New Zealand

Australia's October inflation report on Wednesday will help shape expectations for the Reserve Bank of Australia's December rate decision. In September, annual headline inflation rose to 4.3% and trimmed-mean inflation climbed to 3.6%.

Third-quarter capital spending data due Thursday will show how much businesses invested and whether they revised their spending plans. The RBA will publish its bulletin the same day.

In New Zealand, third-quarter retail sales data due Monday will show how household spending is holding up ahead of the central bank's Dec. 9 rate decision.

South Korea

Bank of Korea is expected to raise its benchmark rate by a quarter-percentage-point to 3.25% on Thursday after leaving it unchanged in October.

Some analysts also expect the bank to raise its growth and inflation forecasts for 2026 and 2027 as demand for chips used in artificial intelligence boosts exports and price pressures persist.

The central bank signaled it would raise its growth forecasts after third-quarter gross domestic product grew faster than expected. It expects inflation to stay above its 2% target through 2027.

The International Monetary Fund, the Korea Development Institute and Citi Research raised their growth forecasts for South Korea earlier this month, citing strength in the semiconductor industry.

Singapore

Singapore's consumer-price index likely rose 1.9% in October from a year earlier, down from 2.2% in September, according to the median estimate of six economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. Core inflation, which excludes private road transport and accommodation costs, likely slowed to 1.6% from 2.0%, the poll showed. The data are due Monday.

Lower fourth-quarter electricity tariffs and a high year-earlier comparison likely helped ease inflation, said UOB economist Jester Koh.

Final third-quarter gross domestic product figures are due Tuesday. An advance estimate showed the economy grew 5.4% from a year earlier. DBS economists expect that figure to be revised up to 5.6%, mainly because manufacturing grew faster than initially reported.

DBS expects the government to forecast growth of 2.5% to 4.5% for 2027.

Any references to days are in local times.

Write to Renae Dyer at renae.dyer@wsj.com and Jihye Lee at jihye.lee@wsj.com

data.title: MetaOptics Ltd Secures up to S$32 Million Share Subscription Facility from GEM Opportunities Fund ISA Ltd.
data.description:
Three-year committed facility provides MetaOptics with flexible growth capital, drawn down at the Company's sole discretion

SINGAPORE, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MetaOptics Ltd (Catalist: 9MT) (OTCQX: MOTLY) ("MetaOptics" or the "Company", and together with its subsidiaries, the "Group"), a Singapore-headquartered semiconductor optics company pioneering glass-based metalens solutions enhanced by AI-driven image processing, announced that it had on 20 November 2026, entered into a share subscription facility agreement with GEM Opportunities Fund ISA Ltd. ("GEM"), the Bermuda-based investment vehicle managed by Global Emerging Markets (GEM), New York, for an aggregate commitment of up to S$32 million (the "Share Subscription Facility"). The Share Subscription Facility is subject to, inter alia, the approval of the Company's shareholders ("Shareholders") at an extraordinary general meeting ("EGM") to be convened. A circular containing further details of the Share Subscription Facility, together with the notice of EGM, will be despatched to Shareholders in due course.

The Company intends to apply the net proceeds from drawdowns under the Share Subscription Facility, entirely for the Group's working capital purposes, including general corporate expenses, funding the day-to-day operations of the Group and supporting the growth of its existing business. As part of the Group's plans to grow its existing business, the Group intends to establish a new 12-inch glass semiconductor fabrication line in the United States to produce metalenses for co-packaged optics ("CPO") and colour imaging applications. The Share Subscription Facility provides MetaOptics with flexible access to growth capital while allowing the Company to control the timing of any drawdowns, in line with its capital needs and prevailing market conditions.

Mr Thng Chong Kim, Executive Chairman of MetaOptics, said: "This Share Subscription Facility gives us a reliable, flexible source of capital for our day-to-day operations and to support the growth of our existing business by establishing a new 12-inch glass semiconductor fabrication line in the United States, on terms that put MetaOptics in control of the timing and size of each drawdown. We are pleased to have the backing of GEM, an experienced global investor, as we execute on our plans and build long-term value for our Shareholders."

This press release should be read in conjunction with the announcement released by the Company on SGXNet on 23 November 2026 in relation to the Share Subscription Facility.

About MetaOptics LtdMetaOptics Ltd (Catalist: 9MT) is a leading-edge semiconductor optics company pioneering glass-based metalens solutions enhanced by AI-driven image processing. Using advanced optical design and a scalable 12-inch DUV lithography process, it powers next-generation applications in CPO, mobile, AR/VR, automotive and other emerging markets. Headquartered in Singapore, MetaOptics aims to deliver high-performance optics with the reliability and scalability demanded by today's most innovative technology brands. Find out more at www.metaoptics.sg.

About GEMGEM (Global Emerging Markets) is a US$3.4 billion alternative investment group with operations in Paris, New York, Los Angeles and the Bahamas. GEM manages a diverse set of investment vehicles focused on emerging and developed markets and has completed over 600 transactions in 75 countries. Each investment vehicle has a different degree of operational control, risk-adjusted return and liquidity profile. Its family of funds and investment vehicles provides GEM and its partners with exposure to Small-Mid Cap Management Buyouts, Private Investments in Public Equities and select venture investments.  For more information, please visit www.gemny.com.

Forward-Looking StatementsThis press release contains forward-looking statements, including statements regarding the share subscription facility, the Company's intended use of proceeds and its business plans. These statements are based on the Company's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. The Facility is subject to shareholder approval at the EGM, and drawdowns under the Facility are subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions and to the execution of definitive documentation. There can be no assurance as to the amount or timing of any funds the Company may ultimately raise. The Company undertakes no obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required by law.

SOURCE METAOPTICS LTD

data.title: South Korea November 1-20 exports surge on chip sales
data.description:
South Korea's exports surged 101.5% in the first 20 days of this month from a year earlier, led by chip sales that almost quadrupled from a year earlier, customs data showed on Wednesday.

Imports increased 39.4%, resulting in preliminary trade balance of $27.11 billion.

Exports of semiconductors increased 294.4%, accounting for 49.7% of the total.
